newsitem.title: USA: Russia reneges on missile agreement, U.S. says.
newsitem.headline: Russia reneges on missile agreement, U.S. says.

text.p: Russia has backed away at the last moment from an agreement on regional missile defences that was set for signing on October 31, U.S. officials said (on) Wednesday.

"This has been called off. There'll be no signing ceremony in Geneva on Thursday...We're disappointed by Russia's reversal of its own position late last week," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.

Another official told Reuters: "We had a set of documents that was agreed by all sides, the texts were confirmed, the translators had certified the documents meant the same thing, we had a time and place (Geneva) for the signing and people were flying in from all (the relevant) capitals. We were all set."

The collapse of the deal that Secretary of State Warren Christopher and Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov reaffirmed in New York on September 23 is a blow to Clinton administration arms control efforts.
It also raises more questions about how the power struggle in Moscow is affecting Russian policy and the ability of the United States and Russia to deal cooperatively.
The agreement announced by Christopher and Primakov last month would specify which short-range defence missile systems are allowed under the 1972 Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty.
